purpose: Regression guard against this codebase's own measured local capacity on the accepted v2 load harness. Not a customer-facing latency/throughput guarantee, and not tuned to any external SLA -- none is defined anywhere in this repository's governance for the SUN-1000 load criterion.
update_policy: A normal `pnpm security:load` run NEVER rewrites this file or loosens any threshold derived from it -- there is no 'learn mode' in ordinary release execution. Updating this baseline is a separate, deliberate, human-reviewed action (a new checkpoint, exactly like this one), requiring fresh measured evidence and an explicit commit reviewing the new numbers against the old ones.

measured_p95_evidence_ms._comment: Worst-observed p95 (ms) across multiple real, unmodified campaigns against the accepted 1N-B harness (same profiles/concurrency/request-counts as committed at 5bc6c4d and unchanged since), collected across this checkpoint and the prior one. Real machine-to-machine/run-to-run variance is visible directly in this evidence (e.g. STEADY_CONCURRENCY ranged ~4012-6367ms across 3 runs) -- this is exactly why a same-run self-normalizing threshold cannot serve as a regression guard, and why the frozen ceilings below use a generous fixed margin over the worst value observed, not the typical one.

official_baseline_freeze_campaign._comment: Full aggregate/per-service evidence from the single official 1N-B2 baseline-freeze campaign (post-instrumentation, pre-threshold-finalization run), dumped by RESOURCE_STABILITY to security/output/load-campaign-metrics.json and copied here for permanent record. Request counts/concurrency unchanged from the accepted 1N-B harness.

frozen_thresholds._derivation: fixed_p95_ceiling_ms = max(worst_observed_p95 * margin, floor_ms). margin=3 (already-observed same-machine run-to-run variance alone reaches ~1.6x for STEADY_CONCURRENCY; a further 3x on top of the WORST observed value, not the typical one, gives ample headroom for CI-machine variability while still catching a genuine multi-x regression). floor_ms=5000 (CI-machine floor, matching 1N-B's original floor rationale, applied uniformly). Values rounded UP to the nearest 500ms for a small extra safety margin -- never rounded down.

throughput_policy: THROUGHPUT_MEASURED_NOT_RELEASE_BLOCKING. Measured throughput (~1.8-2.2 req/s per profile) is recorded as evidence in security/output/load-campaign-metrics.json on every run, but is bounded by this harness's own deliberately-small concurrency settings (2-16) and real per-request cryptographic/D1 work, not by any system-wide capacity ceiling -- no trustworthy cross-machine minimum QPS can be justified from this evidence alone. Latency (this file), correctness (0 unexpected failures/duplicates), and resource-growth guards (RESOURCE_STABILITY, growth < 5x, already a fixed relative bound) are what release-gate this criterion.

resource_guard.note: Already a fixed constant (5x), not derived from any candidate run's own measurement -- retained unchanged at 1N-B2, not part of this checkpoint's correction.
